name: The Millbrook Disappearances
summary: Villagers vanish from Millbrook; a cult of hunger digs beneath Gallows Hill for the first of seven Teeth. Teaches exploration, talk, skill checks, grid combat, rest, shops, companions and travel.

chapters.name: The Millbrook Disappearances
chapters.summary: From the chalked sigil at the well to the altar under Gallows Hill, and onto the road.

scenes.name: Millbrook Green
scenes.seed: Millbrook's green at dusk: shutters slamming one after another, a dog howling at the old well, the chapel bell silent. Four villagers have vanished in two weeks and nobody stays out after dark.

variants.seed: By daylight the village pretends to be normal: carts, chickens, the smell of bread. People still glance at Gallows Hill before they speak.
Word of the barrow has spread. Doors that were barred now stand open, and people nod as you pass.
Ser Corwin walks beside you, still stiff from the chains, greeting every child by name.

onEnter.text: You reach Millbrook as the light goes: shutters slam, a door is barred behind a frightened face, and somewhere a dog will not stop howling at the well.
onEnter.tip: Places of interest in a scene have their own actions. Look around, or type what you want to do in your own words.

pois.name: The Well
pois.seed: An old stone well with a rope-worn lip. Something is chalked on the capstone.

actions.label: Examine the well

outcome.text: Chalked on the capstone: a black mouth ringed with seven teeth. It is fresh — the chalk still smears.
outcome.tip: Clues you find are worth writing down: the Journal button keeps your own notes.

actions.label: Recall what the sigil means (Religion DC 10)

success.text: The mouth and seven teeth: the old mark of Vashkul, the Hungering Dark of the fen-tales. Someone here worships hunger itself.

failure.text: It tugs at a memory of fen-tales and sermons, but the meaning slips away.

actions.label: Study the wet footprints (Investigation DC 12)

success.text: Several people, barefoot, walking in step. The mud on their heels is the grey clay of the barrow on Gallows Hill.

failure.text: Wet prints lead away from the well toward Gallows Hill, but the rain has blurred them.

actions.label: Investigate the scurrying at the well

outcome.text: Something big and grey bolts out from the well's shadow, teeth bared.
outcome.tip: In combat you act on the battle map: move, attack, then End turn. Enemies act in initiative order.

pois.name: Chapel of Solenne
pois.seed: A small chapel of the dawn goddess, candles guttering. A kneeler is worn smooth where someone prays every night.

actions.label: Say a prayer for the missing

outcome.text: The candles steady for a moment. On the kneeler someone has carved four names: Pip, Tobin, Maddy, Moll.

pois.name: Marrow's General Goods
pois.seed: A crooked shopfront with a hand-painted sign. Shuttered at night; by day Widow Marrow's voice carries into the street.

actions.label: Listen to the village (passive Perception)

success.text: Behind a shutter a woman whispers: 'the hill took them, the hill and the hooded brother'.

failure.text: Only the dog and the wind.

actions.label: Wait until morning

outcome.text: You doze on the chapel steps until the sun comes up.

actions.label: Wait until morning

outcome.text: You doze on the chapel steps until the sun comes up.

exits.label: Go into the Plough and Lantern
Follow the tracks toward Gallows Hill
Visit Marrow's shop and the chapel

scenes.name: The Plough and Lantern
scenes.seed: A low, smoky taproom. Reeve Hollis Tamsin drinks alone at the hearth. Miller Oda Hallard weeps in a corner and flinches whenever the door opens.

variants.seed: A big man in a threadbare surcoat of the Dawn Lance is arguing with the Reeve: 'Let me search the hill!' — 'You were dismissed from the Lance, Ashvale. Sit down.'
The taproom is loud with relief. Somebody has pinned the barrow key above the bar like a trophy.

onEnter.text: The knight — Ser Corwin Ashvale — slams a coin on the bar and storms out into the night, toward the hill.
onEnter.tip: Talking can be done with the buttons or in your own words. Skills like Persuasion and Insight are rolled for you, with the math shown in the dice tray.

actions.label: Ask the Reeve for help (Persuasion DC 12)

success.text: The Reeve looks at you properly for the first time. He slides over a list of the missing — and an iron key. 'The old barrow gate. God help you.'
success.tip: Showing evidence (like the sigil) can give you advantage on a check.

failure.text: 'I've buried enough strangers' good intentions,' he mutters, but his hand strays to the key on his belt.

actions.label: Demand the barrow key (Intimidation DC 10)

success.text: The Reeve's face hardens, but he tosses the key onto the table. 'Take it. And don't come back here.'

failure.text: Half the taproom stands up. The Reeve does not move.

actions.label: Pay the Reeve a 5 gp 'deposit' for the key

outcome.text: The coins vanish into his coat. The key clinks onto the table.

actions.label: Watch Miller Oda (Insight DC 13)

success.text: Her grief is real, but so is her guilt: she keeps touching an empty purse.

failure.text: A mother crying for her son. Nothing more to see.

actions.label: Gently ask Oda what she's hiding (Persuasion DC 11)

success.text: 'A hooded brother came down from the hill. He paid me to leave the mill after dark — he wanted the grain from my stones. I didn't know he'd take Pip!'

failure.text: She shakes her head and hides her face.

actions.label: Pick a fight with the loudmouths at the bar

outcome.text: Two farmhands are only too happy to oblige. Fists only.

actions.label: Sleep in the room the Reeve pays for (long rest)

success.text: In the night the black Tooth whispers. A woman's voice, cultured and sad, sings: 'you will never want again.' You remember every note.
success.tip: A long rest restores Hit Points, Hit Dice and spell slots. Level up from your character card when you have enough XP.

failure.text: You wake before dawn, shaking, the words 'never want again' still in your ears.

actions.label: Rent a room for 5 sp and sleep (long rest)

success.text: In the night the black Tooth whispers. A woman's voice, cultured and sad, sings: 'you will never want again.' You remember every note.

failure.text: You wake before dawn, shaking, the words 'never want again' still in your ears.

exits.label: Step back out onto the green

scenes.name: Gallows Hill Track
scenes.seed: A muddy track along the flooded millrace, through bramble, up to a grassy mound crowned with an old gibbet. Two hooded figures keep watch on the barrow mound.

variants.seed: A bone chime rattles on the mound. The lookouts are gone — inside, and waiting.

actions.label: Follow the barefoot tracks (Survival DC 12)

success.text: The tracks lead true, along the millrace to a ford.
success.tip: Some checks have advantage when you know more — the missing list names where Pip was taken.

failure.text: You lose the trail in the bramble and cast about for an hour. Something whines in the dark — stirges.

advantageIf.source: the missing list names the spot

actions.label: Wade the millrace (Athletics DC 10)

success.text: You brace against the current and make the far bank.

failure.text: The current knocks you against the stones before you haul yourself out, soaked.

actions.label: Hop across on the stones (Acrobatics DC 12)

success.text: Stone to stone, dry-footed.

failure.text: A stone rolls; you land hard in the shallows.

actions.label: Creep up on the barrow (Stealth DC 13)

success.text: You slip past the lookouts' backs to the barrow door. They never turn.

failure.text: A twig snaps. A lookout shakes a bone chime and both vanish into the barrow. They know you're coming.

exits.label: Unlock the barrow gate and go in

success.text: The rusted gate gives with a shriek.

failure.text: The gate holds. Perhaps the Reeve has a key.

scenes.name: Barrow: Root Hall
scenes.seed: A long hall of packed earth and old stone, split by roots as thick as a man. Rats the size of dogs scatter from the torchlight — then turn.

onEnter.text: Three giant rats come at you through the roots.
onEnter.tip: Roots are difficult terrain (double movement). Leaving an enemy's reach provokes an Opportunity Attack.

scenes.name: Barrow: Sheaf Crypt
scenes.seed: Stone niches full of old grain-offerings. A big man hangs in chains against the far wall, beaten bloody: Ser Corwin.

variants.seed: Two cultists crouch over a brazier with their backs to you — they have not heard you.
Two cultists wait behind a barricade of coffin-lids.
You are chained beside Corwin. Your gear lies on a table across the room.

actions.label: Unchain the knight

outcome.text: Corwin sags into your arms. 'They took the children to the altar. Go — I'll follow if I can stand.'

actions.label: Bind your wounds with Corwin (short rest)

outcome.text: Corwin tears his surcoat into bandages. 'Again, then. Together.'

actions.label: Work the chains loose (Strength DC 12)

success.text: The old staple tears out of the wall.

failure.text: Your wrists bleed, but after a long while Corwin works both your chains loose.

scenes.name: Barrow: The Tithe Altar
scenes.seed: A round chamber around a stone altar carved like a jaw. Four captives are chained to it — a boy in a miller's smock, a shepherd, two small twin girls. In the altar's basin sits a black, tooth-shaped stone that drinks the torchlight.

variants.seed: The altar is quiet now. The captives stare at the black Tooth as if it might bite.

actions.label: Face the cultists at the altar again

outcome.text: The cult is waiting, and so is the altar.

actions.label: Break the captives' chains before the altar feeds again (Athletics DC 12)

success.text: Link after link gives. Everyone still chained walks out alive, Pip first.

failure.text: You free Pip and the twins — but the shepherd Tobin has stopped breathing by the time his chain breaks.

actions.label: Pick the shackles with thieves' tools (Dexterity DC 12)

success.text: Click, click, click, click. Everyone still chained walks out alive.

failure.text: The picks slip in your sweating fingers; by the time the last lock opens, Tobin is gone.

actions.label: Chase Brother Ashby into the collapsing tunnel (Athletics DC 13)

success.text: You tackle him in the dark as the roof comes down behind you. Brother Ashby is your prisoner.

failure.text: Earth pours down between you. His laughter fades into the hill.

actions.label: Cut Brother Ashby down before he reaches the tunnel

outcome.text: Ashby falls across the altar's lip. The captives watch in silence.

actions.label: Let Ashby flee — the captives matter more

outcome.text: He is gone into the dark. The captives are what matter.

exits.label: Carry the rescued to the little shrine above

scenes.name: Shrine of Thaloren
scenes.seed: A small shrine off the barrow's upper hall: an antler-brazier cold for centuries, a carved stag on the wall. The rescued villagers huddle here, too weak to walk.

variants.seed: The antler-brazier burns with a clean green flame. The dark feels further away.

onEnter.text: Corwin limps in behind you and sits heavily against the wall.
onEnter.tip: A short rest (1 hour) lets you spend Hit Dice to heal. Rests are only safe in safe places.

actions.label: Rekindle the antler-brazier (Religion DC 10)

success.text: You speak the old harvest-words and the brazier catches.

failure.text: The words won't come; the brazier stays cold.

actions.label: Coax a fire from the old tinder (Nature DC 12)

success.text: Dry moss, patience, and the brazier catches.

failure.text: The tinder is rotten through.

actions.label: Take a short rest by the fire

outcome.text: An hour by the green flame. Even the twins sleep.

actions.label: Take a short rest in the dark

outcome.text: You settle in the dark — and the rats come back for the scraps.

scenes.name: Marrow's Goods and the Chapel
scenes.seed: Widow Agna Marrow's cluttered shop — potions, rope, a chain shirt on a dummy — and across the lane the Chapel of Solenne, where Ser Corwin kneels at the altar.

onEnter.tip: Open the shop from the menu bar to buy, sell and haggle. Stock is limited and prices depend on your reputation.

actions.label: Return Widow Marrow's stolen ring

outcome.text: She turns the ring over and over, then presses a potion into your hand. 'My Harl's ring. Anything you need, you ask me first.'

actions.label: Ask Corwin to ride with you

outcome.text: 'The Choir took children from under my nose. I will not wait for the Lance's permission.' He rises and offers his hand.
outcome.tip: Companions fight beside you. On their party card you can switch who controls them in combat: the AI or you.

actions.label: Ask Corwin to ride with you (Persuasion DC 10)

success.text: He looks at you a long moment. 'Ashby deserved a trial. But the children need us.' He comes.

failure.text: 'I'll come. But I'll be watching how you use that blade.'

actions.label: Ask why the Lance dismissed him (Insight DC 12)

success.text: He struck a captain who ordered a plague village abandoned to the fen. He would do it again.

failure.text: 'A disagreement over orders,' he says, and changes the subject.

actions.label: Set out alone

outcome.text: The road is yours alone.

scenes.name: The South Road
scenes.seed: The Reeve walks you to the milestone at the edge of the village. 'That black thing is unholy. Someone must take it where it can be kept.' Two roads: east to Ravensgate and the Lantern Wardens, who know fen-evil; or south to Brightwater and the Crown's magistrate, the proper authority.

variants.seed: The Reeve won't come. It is Corwin who walks you to the milestone and says the words.

onEnter.tip: The world map (Map button) shows known places, routes and travel time by pace. Slow is safer; fast gets you there sooner but careless.

actions.label: Take the east road to Ravensgate (30 miles)
Take the south road to Brightwater (25 miles)

scenes.name: Barley Fields at Dusk
scenes.seed: Barley rustles on both sides of the road as the light fails. Something moves through it, low and fast, circling.

onEnter.text: Two wolves break from the barley.

actions.label: Walk on to the gates of Ravensgate

outcome.text: Ravensgate's black walls rise over the last dry ridge before the fen. The gates are sealed against the plague — and a Warden-Sergeant is looking for outsiders who aren't sick yet.

scenes.name: The Toll Bridge
scenes.seed: A plank bridge over the Brightwater, and two hard-faced men with a chain across it. 'Toll's five gold. Road repairs.' There have been no repairs.

actions.label: Pay the 5 gp toll

outcome.text: They drop the chain with mock bows.

actions.label: Talk them out of it (Persuasion DC 12)

success.text: After a moment's thought about the knight — or the look in your eye — they decide the toll is waived today.

failure.text: 'Five gold, or the river.'

actions.label: Clear the bridge by force

outcome.text: They draw.

actions.label: Hand the Tooth to the magistrate's clerk

outcome.text: The clerk wraps the black Tooth in silk, seals the box with the Royal Almonry's wheat-and-crown, and 'forwards it for safekeeping'. He gives you a crown writ for Ravensgate: the plague's source wants investigating.

actions.label: Keep the Tooth and ask only for a writ

outcome.text: The magistrate grumbles, but signs a crown writ sending you to Ravensgate to find the plague's source.

npcs.name: Reeve Hollis Tamsin
npcs.personality: Tired, honest and proud; ashamed he cannot protect his village.
secrets: He keeps the only key to the old barrow gate.

npcs.name: Miller Oda Hallard
npcs.personality: Frightened mother; guilt makes her snappish.
secrets: She took coin from a 'hooded brother' to leave her mill after dark.

npcs.name: Widow Agna Marrow
npcs.personality: Sharp, gossip-hungry, a hard haggler with a soft heart she hides.
secrets: The cultists stole her dead husband's ring from the shop.

npcs.name: Ser Corwin Ashvale
npcs.personality: Earnest, stubborn and dry-humoured; ashamed of his dismissal but never mopes.
npcs.voice: Deep, measured, a soldier's clipped courtesy.
secrets: He was dismissed from the Dawn Lance for striking a captain who ordered a plague village abandoned.

npcs.name: Brother Ashby
npcs.personality: Soft-spoken, fervent former sexton; believes hunger can be ended.

win.text: The rat squeals and vanishes down the well shaft.

lose.text: You come round at the well's edge with a bitten ankle; the rat is long gone.

win.text: The farmhands buy you a drink afterwards. Millbrook respects a good fight.

lose.text: You wake in the tavern stable, lighter by some coin and all your dignity.

win.text: The last stirge drops into the bramble.

lose.text: The Reeve's search party finds you at dawn, pale and bitten. The cultists have moved one captive deeper.

win.text: The last rat thrashes and lies still among the roots.

lose.text: You crawl back out of the barrow to the gibbet, bleeding. The children are still down there.

win.text: The second cultist falls against the niches, spilling grain.

lose.text: You wake chained beside Ser Corwin. Your gear is on a table across the room.

win.text: Brother Ashby, bleeding, backs toward a collapsing tunnel behind the altar. Among the cult's things: 25 gold, a healing potion, a sickle — and a woman's ring engraved 'A. & H.'

lose.text: You wake chained in the crypt beside Corwin. Ashby has fled with one of the captives.

win.text: Brother Ashby, bleeding, backs toward a collapsing tunnel behind the altar. Among the cult's things: 25 gold, a healing potion, a sickle — and a woman's ring engraved 'A. & H.'

lose.text: You wake chained in the crypt beside Corwin. Ashby has fled with one of the captives.

win.text: With the rats gone you rest at last.

lose.text: You drive them off at last, bloodied, and rest where you fall.

win.text: The wolves limp back into the barley.

flee.text: You run for the road and the wolves lose interest at the ditch.

lose.text: You wake on the roadside at dawn; your purse is lighter, but the black Tooth lies untouched where it fell — the robbers who found you fled from it.

win.text: The chain rattles into the river after them.

lose.text: You wake on the bank at dawn, robbed. They left the black Tooth — none of them would touch it.

beats.text: The captives are chained to the altar, and it is feeding.
They were waiting: the rats come boiling out of the altar's jaw.
Four children and a shepherd walk out of the barrow.
The Reeve's report to the Crown will speak well of you.
Corwin will not stop talking about the children you brought home.

objectives.text: Find out what is taking the villagers
Get into the barrow on Gallows Hill
Reach the altar and stop the feeding
See Widow Marrow and Ser Corwin in the village by day
Take the Tooth somewhere it can be kept

endings.name: To Ravensgate
endings.text: Warden-Sergeant Odo Brask needs outsiders who aren't sick yet to go into Hollowmere, where the sick hear the same voice you heard in the barrow. The Whispering Fen is waiting.

endings.name: Sent to Ravensgate
endings.text: With a crown writ in your pack you take the fen road to Ravensgate, where the plague is said to begin. The Whispering Fen is waiting.
